your_book:
Jaleel's book ended Friday modestly bruised but largely intact, with the overall unrealized gain holding at +6.74%. The session's damage was concentrated in a handful of names: Broadcom (AVGO) was the standout laggard, sliding –5.94% — a significant single-day move, even if the position is a small ~1.5% weight. The headline driver appears to be Stanley Druckenmiller's Q2 13-F showing a full exit of AVGO, which rattled sentiment across the semi complex. Zoetis (ZTS) also had a rough Friday, dropping –2.7%, deepening its already negative unrealized gain of –6.3% — and that's the book's third-largest position at 9.6%. ServiceNow (NOW) and Adobe (ADBE) each fell around –2.5%, adding to the tech-software drag. On the positive side, little stood out: Rocket Lab (RKLB) and Neurocrine Biosciences (NBIX) posted modest gains of +0.19% and +1.26% respectively, but neither moves the needle given their weights.

The drift worth flagging is ZTS: rated STRONG BUY with a QARP score of 75.4, yet sitting –6.3% in the red and losing ground on Friday. That's a widening gap between the model's conviction and price reality — worth monitoring to see if the thesis is simply early or quietly breaking down. Similarly, LULU carries a –6.5% unrealized loss against a BUY verdict, with a guidance cut already on record and the next catalyst not until September 2. BSX, despite a BUY rating and a +7.0% gain, has a flagged guidance slash — growth cut from 10.5% to 7–8.5% — suggesting the current gain may be pricing in a rosier scenario than management is guiding. RKLB remains the structural concern: the book's largest single position at 15.8%, rated AVOID with the weakest QARP score in the portfolio at 36.6.

Into next week, the focus should be NVDA ahead of its August 26 event window — the WSJ report of Nvidia downsizing its $250B OpenAI data center commitment is a material narrative shift, and the stock is sitting on a +22.7% gain. Any further export-control news or AI-capex doubt could pressure that cushion fast. ADBE's –2.39% Friday move on what appears to be a positive peer-news day (software broadly higher on rate sentiment) is an amber signal — if the stock can't rally when the tape is friendly, the AI-disruption narrative is doing real damage ahead of its September 10 report.

attention.headline: Largest position rated AVOID with lowest QARP in book
attention.note: At 15.8% weight, RKLB is the single biggest concentration risk in a capital-preservation portfolio, yet it carries an AVOID verdict and a QARP of just 36.6 — the lowest by a wide margin — making this a size-versus-thesis mismatch that demands a clear rationale or a trim decision.

attention.note: A high-profile institutional exit reported in Q2 13-F filings hit AVGO hard on Friday; while the position is small (~1.5%), the HOLD-QUAL verdict and weakest QARP among the semi names (64.9) make this worth scrutinizing before the narrative worsens further.
